decisions.reason: The REST API documentation lists several distinct resource categories (Agents, Endpoints, Events, Freeform Topics, Webhooks) each with multiple operations, plus a separate Lookup API and Reporting API rate limit section, indicating more than a handful of endpoints but not hundreds, so moderate fits better than unknown.

evidence.snippet:
Gladly API uses token-based
Basic Authentication
. API tokens are associated with designated Gladly users.

decisions.reason: The developer docs explicitly and unambiguously state the API uses token-based Basic Authentication with the HTTP Authorization scheme 'basic', not Bearer.

evidence.snippet: Gladly Administrators can set API permissions on an agent-by-agent basis.
To create and use an API token, your user must have the API User permission.

As an Administrator,
create a user
to use explicitly to create and attach webhooks or tokens.

decisions.reason: Both the developer docs and help docs show that only a Gladly Administrator can grant the API User permission/role needed to create tokens, making admin approval the key friction point rather than a formal app review process (no mention of app review anywhere in the pages).

evidence.snippet: Gladly Administrators can set API permissions on an agent-by-agent basis.
API tokens are required to use Gladly APIs for security and authentication purposes.

decisions.reason: A fully documented REST API with an OpenAPI spec exists and tokens can be self-generated once a user has the API User permission, so the API is buildable but with the caveat that an admin must grant that permission first, matching ready_with_caveats rather than blocked (no evidence of a vendor app-review gate or complete inability to access).
